newsitem.title: USA: U.S. wheat sold to Iraq, first since '89/90 - USDA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. wheat sold to Iraq, first since '89/90 - USDA.

text.p: Iraq bought 50,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat in the week ended March 20 for the first time since the 1989/90 marketing year, U.S. Agriculture Department said Thursday in its weekly export sales report.

The sale comes under a United Nations-monitored oil-for-food deal. The deal allowing oil sales by Iraq worth $2 billion in six months is designed to ease the effect of trade sanctions imposed on Iraq for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
Iraq had been a major customer for U.S. wheat before the trade embargo. It purchased 1.3 million tonnes of U.S. wheat in 1989/90, ranking it as the number eight customer, according to USDA.
Iraq traditionally imported two million to three million tonnes of wheat to meet domestic needs, said USDA analyst Mike Kurtzig, and the U.S. captured about a third of the market.
Kurtzig said Iraq increased its wheat production by about 50 percent during the 1990s but predicted the country would still be a big customer should the trade sanctions be lifted.
"They need wheat, they need feedgrains...We are a very large supplier of so many bulk items that they import," he said.
